Unicode — 16 bits
Unicode is a character standard, not a fixed 16-bit encoding. UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 encode it differently.
GPT: 128 partitions; MBR: 2 TB
128 is a common Windows default, not a universal GPT maximum. The usual MBR 2 TiB limit assumes 512-byte logical sectors. LVM/RAID are not a mandatory linear stack.
3×8⁻²=3/64=0.046875, so the exact value is 101.296875. 101.3 is only a rounded value.
2’s complement of −108; no final carry means negative
The shown 10010100 is the 8-bit representation of −108, obtained by negating +108. Negating the encoded −108 gives +108. Signed subtraction requires overflow checks; carry-out alone is insufficient.
Unicode uses 16 bits; Excess-3 of 1010
Unicode is not fixed-width. The string 1010 is ambiguous: binary 1010 means decimal 10; decimal digits 1010 produce four Excess-3 groups. The calculator requires decimal digits explicitly.
10110 has two 1s and is even; ASCII Delta begins 68
10110 contains THREE 1s: even parity fails. ASCII D is hex 44 (decimal 68), not hex 68. Parity detects any odd number of bit errors, but misses even numbers.
AB′+AC+BC is already minimal
AC is the consensus term of AB′ and BC: AB′+AC+BC = AB′+BC. This is checked over all 8 input combinations.
Worked example 1 grouping prose merges m6,m14 into BD
BD′ is supported by the four-cell group {4,6,12,14}; BC′ by {4,5,12,13}; A′C′D by {1,5}. The printed final answer is consistent, but parts of the grouping prose are not.
A>B is true for these ten; m4,m12 can enlarge with m13 to A0B1′
Only SIX of the 16 combinations have A>B. The listed minterms are correct. The proposed enlargement is invalid: it would include m5 (01>01), which is false. Retain A0B1′B0′.
8086 first 16-bit processor
8086 was Intel’s first 16-bit x86 processor; 16-bit processors existed before it. 8085 clock ratings vary by model.
Macro under 10 instructions; timer 1/12, counter 1/24
Instruction count is a heuristic, not a rule. The timing ratios apply to a classic 12-clock 8051, not every processor or microcontroller.
Agile iteration 1–3 weeks; Agile does not recommend prototypes
Iteration length varies. Scrum allows sprints of one month or less. Agile can use prototypes and does not prohibit them.
White box slowest, black box fastest; white box developer only
Test speed and tester role are not fixed by box type. Both developers and test engineers can use these techniques.
Verification: Are we developing the right product? Validation: Is the developed product right?
Standard mnemonic: verification = building the product right (specification); validation = building the right product (user need). The source table reverses the slogans.
Parity detects single-bit errors only
Parity detects all odd-count bit errors, including a single-bit error, but not all multi-bit errors.
